{{short description|Functional analysis theorem}}
In [[functional analysis]], '''Rådström's embedding theorem''' is a result related to the set of [[Compact space|compact]] and [[Convex set|convex]] subsets of a [[normed vector space]]. It states that such sets can be [[isometry|isometrically]]  [[embedding|embededded]] into a [[convex cone]] in another normed vector space.

The theorem is an important result in that it shows that this family of sets has natural [[linear algebra|linear]] and [[metric space|metric]] structures, which allows for simpler algebraic manipulations via the embedding. It was first proven by [[Hans Rådström]] in 1952.<ref name = "radstrom1952">{{cite journal |last1=Rådström |first1=Hans |author1-link=Hans Rådström |title=An embedding theorem for spaces of convex sets |journal=Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society |date=1952 |volume=3 |pages=165–169 |doi=10.1090/S0002-9939-1952-0045938-2 |url=https://www.ams.org/journals/proc/1952-003-01/S0002-9939-1952-0045938-2/}}</ref>

An extension of Rådström's result to [[locally convex topological vector space]]s, known as the '''Hörmander embedding theorem''', was proven by [[Lars Hörmander]] in 1954.<ref name = "hormander1955">{{cite journal |last1=Hörmander |first1=Lars |author1-link=Lars Hörmander |title=Sur la fonction d'appui des ensembles convexes dans un espace localement convexe |journal=Arkiv för Matematik |date=1955 |volume=3 |issue=12 |pages=181–186 |doi=10.1007/BF02589354}}</ref>

== Preliminaries ==

=== <math>CK(X)</math> and the Hausdorff metric ===

For any [[normed vector space]] <math>(X, || \cdot ||)</math>, let <math>CK(X)</math> be the set of all its convex and compact subsets. We can endow <math>CK(X)</math> with a metric structure given by the [[Hausdorff metric]]

:<math>d_H(A, B) = \sup_{x \in X} |d(x, A) - d(x, B)|,</math>

where <math>d</math> is the metric over <math>X</math> induced by the norm <math>|| \cdot ||</math>, and <math>d(x, Y) = \inf_{y \in Y} d(x, y)</math> is the distance from <math>x</math> to a set <math>Y \subseteq X</math>. It is well known that <math>(CK(X), d_H)</math> forms a [[metric space]] of its own right.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Searcóid |first1=Mícheál Ó |title=Metric Spaces |date=2007 |publisher=Springer |location=London |isbn=978-1-84628-369-7 |page=105 |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-1-84628-627-8}}</ref>

== Theorem ==

=== Main version ===

The main version of Rådström's theorem reads as follows:<ref name = "radstrom1952" /><ref name = "fox2020">{{cite web |last1=Fox |first1=Logan S. | date = 2020 |title=The Embedding Theorems of Rådström and Hörmander |url=https://joelshapiro.org/Pubvit/Downloads/fox_embedding_notes.pdf |website=Logan S. Fox's lecture notes |access-date=25 November 2025}}</ref>

'''Theorem (Rådström, 1952):''' Let <math>(X, || \cdot||)</math> be a normed space. Then there exists a normed space <math>(Y, ||\cdot||_Y)</math> such that the space <math>(CK(X), d_H)</math> can be isometrically embedded into a convex cone <math>C \subseteq Y</math>. Furthermore, it is possible to construct a "minimal" <math>Y</math> for which this holds.{{r|g=nb|r= Minimal in the sense that for any other normed space <math>(Z, ||\cdot||_Z)</math> into which <math>(CK(X), d_H)</math> can be embedded, <math>(Y, ||\cdot||_Y)</math> can also be embedded into a subspace of <math>(Z, ||\cdot||_Z)</math> in which <math>(CK(X), d_H)</math> was embedded.}}

=== Extensions ===

It is possible to generalize Rådström's theorem to [[locally convex topological vector space]]s (LCTVS). This is done via Hörmander's embedding theorem, proven by [[Lars Hörmander]] in 1954.<ref name = "hormander1955" /> Hörmander's theorem explicitly constructs an embedding via [[support function]]s of closed, convex, [[Bounded set (topological vector space)|(strongly) bounded]]  sets.

'''Theorem (Hörmander, 1954):''' let <math>X</math> be a real [[LCTVS]], and <math>CB(X)</math> the set of all its closed, convex, [[Bounded set (topological vector space)|(strongly) bounded]] subsets. Denoting by <math>X^*</math> the [[dual space]] of <math>X</math>, consider the closed unit ball <math>\mathcal B^* \subseteq X^*</math>, and the [[Banach space]] <math>\mathcal C_b (\mathcal B^*)</math> of all continuous, bounded functions <math>h :B^* \to \mathbb R</math>. For each <math>A \in CB(X)</math>, let <math>s_A \in \mathcal C_b (\mathcal B^*)</math> defined by

:<math>s_A(x) = \sup_{y \in A} \langle x, y\rangle</math>

be its [[support function]]. Then the mapping <math>H: CB(X) \to \mathcal C_b(\mathcal B^*)</math> given by

:<math>A \mapsto s_A</math>

is an isometric embedding into a convex cone in <math>\mathcal C_b(\mathcal B^*)</math>. Moreover, by the [[Support function#Properties|properties of support functions]] such embedding is also [[linear map|linear]] when <math>CB(X)</math> is endowed with a [[vector space|vector-space structure]] given by the [[Minkowski sum]] and scalar multiplication.<ref name = "fox2020" />

== Applications ==

=== Integration of set-valued functions ===

The theorem can be used to define the [[Integral of a correspondence|integral of a set-valued function]] (or [[Set-valued function|correspondence]]) via [[Integral of a correspondence#The Debreu integral|Debreu's integral]].<ref name = "debreu1967">{{cite book |last1=Debreu |first1=Gérard |author1-link=Gérard Debreu |editor1-last=Le Cam |editor1-first=Lucien |editor2-last=Neyman |editor2-first=Jerzy |editor1-link=Lucien Le Cam |editor2-link=Jerzy Neyman |title=Proceedings of the Fifth Berkeley Symposium on Mathematical Statistics and Probability, Volume 2: Contributions to Probability Theory, Part 1 |date=1967 |publisher=University of California Press |isbn=978-0520366701 |pages=351–372 |chapter=Integration of Correspondences}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Cerreia-Vioglio |first1=Simone |last2=Ok |first2=Efe A. |title=Abstract integration of set-valued functions |journal=Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications |date=2025 |volume=547 |issue=2 |doi=10.1016/j.jmaa.2024.129169}}</ref> This has applications, for example, in the theory of [[random compact set]]s.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Artstein |first1=Zvi |last2=Vitale |first2=Richard A. |title=A Strong Law of Large Numbers for Random Compact Sets |journal=Annals of Probability |volume=3 |issue=5 |pages=879–882 |doi=10.1214/aop/1176996275}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Artstein |first1=Zvi |last2=Burns |first2=John Allen |title=Integration of compact set-valued functions |journal=Pacific Journal of Mathematics |volume=58 |issue=2 |pages=297–307 |doi=10.2140/pjm.1975.58.297}}</ref>
